notes.title: A New Beginning - Game Update #1
notes.notes:
We’ve got some exciting updates to share as we continue rebuilding the game from the ground up

Shane’s New Look 
Shane just got a major overhaul with a fresh model, a more refined rig, and enhanced animations! We’ve integrated the latest motion-matching tech from Unreal Engine 5 to give you tighter, more responsive control over your hero.

Multiplayer Replication Solved
We encountered some challenges getting multiplayer systems to sync properly, but our talented dev team worked through them. Now, everything runs smoothly across multiplayer, making the experience feel seamless.

Core Gameplay Progress
We’ve been hard at work building the foundation of the gameplay using Unreal’s Ability System, which gives us the flexibility to create complex hero abilities. The first big milestone is that the ball and its mechanics are fully 
functional! 🎉

New Game Mode in Development
Our team is also developing an exciting new game mode that promises to be fast-paced, dynamic, and more engaging than ever. We’ll share more details soon!

What’s Next?
Coming up, we’re focused on making Shane interact with the ball by bringing his Vinewall skill to life, adding the ability to throw the ball, and introducing a volley hit mechanic for extra intensity.

notes.title: A New Beginning - Game Update #3
notes.notes:
This week, we’ve been brainstorming the new map layout!

Map Concept
Each team will start next to their own Guardian, with two main paths to choose from:
1️⃣ Water Path: A shorter route that takes you through water, but it’ll slow your movement down.
2️⃣ Bridge Path: A longer route, but you avoid the slow-down effect, allowing for faster positioning.

The ball will spawn in the center of the map, encouraging both teams to strategize their approach early and fight for control. The map will be filled with various tiles to create more dynamic and unpredictable gameplay moments.

Buffs & Power-Ups
We’ll also be spreading XP and Power Buffs across the map, giving players more reasons to explore and control key areas.

Guardian Weak Spots
Each team’s main Guardian will have weak spots that must be deactivated before it can be defeated. This will add another layer of strategy to the game and make for intense battles!

notes.title: A New Beginning - Game Update #2
notes.notes:
Here’s what we’ve been working on this week

Shane’s clothing is getting some work done to make it more dynamic, we are adding rigid body simulation to give it a more natural and overlapping feel.

We’ve added the throw ability functionality, but we ran into a strange bug with the animation. After investigating, we discovered we needed to create a custom montage node to play our animations properly in a replicated way alongside the motion-matching system. It’s a work in progress, but we're hoping to have it resolved by next week! 

We’ve also been working on getting Shane’s Vinewall ability functional
which will serve as a base for creating other abilities that require a preview.

As part of making the game more scalable and to take full advantage of Unreal's Gameplay Ability System (GAS), we’ve started moving more information and data into Data Assets. For those unfamiliar, Data Assets are reusable data containers in Unreal that allow us to store important gameplay variables and properties in one place. The best part? We’ve integrated them into the game in real time, so we can quickly tweak and test things without needing to dive into code.

On the game mode side, we’ve started testing a new Tile System. This system lets players interact with tiles on the field, creating more dynamic gameplay moments.. It’s been so much fun that we had trouble stopping the recording.

We’re also developing a Guardian Game Mode! Instead of the usual 5-minute timed matches, players will need to defeat a Guardian to win. How do you hit the Guardian, you ask? You’ll need to charge up the ball by making successful passes, then target the Guardian’s weak spots to deal damage.

Our goal is to get the core mechanics in place as quickly as possible so you can jump in and test it with us. We’re eager to hear your feedback and use it to improve the game!

Thanks for all the support, and we’ll see you next week! 💬

notes.title: A New Begining - Game Update #4
notes.notes:
This week, we focused on three main areas: HUD brainstorming, animation fixes, and enhancing the Tile System!

HUD Brainstorming
We spent some time brainstorming our HUD design. We listed out each element we needed and explored an amazing site that showcases various game UIs to draw inspiration. We had a great debate on what the HUD should look like and what elements it should have. Stay tuned for more on this as we lock down our design!

Animation System Update
Remember that annoying animation bug we mentioned last time? It turns out we had to redo the motion-matching system again! This time, we tackled it without real-time retargeting, and while it took some time, the blend animations are now working properly. We’ve got a few new bugs to squash, but it’s a step forward!

Tile System Progress
We’re super excited about the Tile System! We’re starting to see sparks of cool gameplay moments emerging from it. Here’s how it works:

Each player earns tile points through various actions like passing the ball, hitting the Guardian, or leveling up. These points can be used to activate tiles on the field, triggering different effects like Jump Pads, Ice Tiles, or even walls! The goal is to make the map more dynamic and create unique moments in every match.
Got some cool ideas for new tile effects? let us know!
